name: Axion 1.0-35B
context_scaling: config.json text_config max_position_embeddings 262144 (no rope_scaling key; rope_parameters rope_theta 1e7 with partial_rotary_factor 0.25 and mrope_interleaved true). The card's own serving example passes --max-model-len 131072, so the documented served length is half the config ceiling. No long-context eval is printed.
attention_variant: Hybrid linear/full attention (qwen3_5_moe): 40 layers, 30 linear_attention and 10 full_attention at indices 3,7,11,...,39 (one per four). Full layers use GQA 16 query heads x 2 KV heads, head_dim 256; linear layers use 16 key heads / 32 value heads at 128 dims with linear_conv_kernel_dim 4. Gated attention (attn_output_gate true).
notes: ADDED 2026-11-10 from the trending crawl (p2 of trendingScore, 1,125 downloads / 70 likes; repo created 2026-10-16). WHAT IT IS: NOT a first-party base model. The repo is titled 'Axion 1.0-35B - Reproduction': a checkpoint reproducing the recipe in arXiv 2611.03233 ('Axion 1.0: Open Agent Foundation Models, Simplified'), whose author list the card prints as Yuqi Jia et al. and whose code link points at github.com/bytedance/axion1_0. It is therefore recorded with base_model null and derivative_kind null - the geometry is Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-shaped but the card claims training from scratch through the paper's three stages, not a post-train of a Qwen checkpoint, so labelling it a finetune would be a guess. PARAMS: safetensors.total 35,107,181,936 -> params_b 35.107, matching the Qwen3.5-35B-A3B tensor count almost exactly (35,107,181,936 is the same figure clingeek-35b-a3b and ising-calibration-1-35b-a3b carry). active_params_b 3.0 is the card's own 'approximately 35B total, 3B active' figure, not re-derived. DERIVED (arithmetic): kv_cache_bytes_per_token = 10 full_attention layers x 2 KV heads x 256 head_dim x 2 (K and V) x 2 bytes = 20,480 bytes/token. The 30 linear_attention layers hold constant-size recurrent state, NOT a per-token cache, so they are excluded - including them would have inflated this 4x. flops_per_token_active = 2 x 3.0e9 = 6.0e9. HARDWARE GATE: PASSES. active 3.0B <= 40, and 35.107 x 0.5 GiB = 17.6 GiB at 4-bit, far under the 128 GiB budget; the 20 KB/token KV means 128K context adds only ~2.6 GB of cache because 30 of 40 layers are linear. This is exactly the offload-friendly shape the catalog prefers. WHAT IT EVIDENCES: the card prints paper-vs-reproduction side by side, which makes the delta auditable: +0.6 HLE, 0.0 BMB, -1.8 SEAL-0, +0.2 HiPhO, -1.0 FS Olympiad, -1.7 FS Research. Three of six rows are degraded, three are equal or better. The headline claims are HLE 52.8 and SEAL-0 60.4, both best-in-row among sub-40B-active models the catalog tracks. CAVEATS: (1) all six rows are vendor claims from the reproducing authors, and the paper's numbers are the recipe authors'; the 'wins' are against the card's chosen baseline columns, not an independent harness. (2) Every frontier comparator in the table except Agents-A1 is a closed model with no card. (3) The card states eight GPUs and tensor-parallel 8 for the documented serve command, so the smallest published configuration is 8x H-class hardware - record it as a contender, not a single-box run. (4) The task is scientific reasoning, so these rows say nothing about chat or agentic coding; the card prints no SWE or Terminal-Bench number at all.

benchmarks.name: HLE
benchmarks.config: Card table 'Performance' (paper-reported beside reproduction), row Axion 1.0-35B. Accuracy on full Humanity's Last Exam. The reproduction column prints 52.8 vs the paper's 52.2, so the released checkpoint is 0.6pp ABOVE the paper - unusual and worth flagging, because it means the delta is not a degradation. WINS vs the catalog's previous best at <=40B active on HLE: xyz-aquila-mini 51.1 (+1.7pp) and bigbang-v1 50.3; LOSSES to glm-5-3-flash 55.3 but that model is 18B active and 320B total on a different card. Beats Agents-A1 47.6, DeepSeek-V4-Pro Preview 48.2, Gemini 3.1 Pro 51.4 and GPT-5.5 52.2 in the same table.

benchmarks.name: SEAL-0
benchmarks.config: Same table, row SEAL-0. Reproduction 60.4 vs paper 62.2 - the one row where the released checkpoint LOSES ground (-1.8pp), recorded deliberately. Still WINS the row by a wide margin: Agents-A1 56.4, DeepSeek-V4-Pro Preview 55.0, Kimi-K2.6 50.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro 53.2, GPT-5.6 Sol 53.2, GPT-5.5 42.3. SEAL-0 previously had no row anywhere in the catalog, so this is a first datapoint rather than a beaten best.

benchmarks.name: HiPhO
benchmarks.config: Same table, row HiPhO. Reproduction 45.9 vs paper 45.7 (+0.2pp). WINS vs GPT-5.5 43.3, GPT-5.6 Sol 42.9, Kimi-K2.6 41.1, DeepSeek-V4-Pro Preview 38.7 and Gemini 3.1 Pro 38.5. LOSSES recorded: Agents-A1 prints 46.4, i.e. -0.5pp. Against the catalog it beats sage-a1-5 45.3, the only other HiPhO row, by 0.6pp - but sage-a1-5 is also ~3B active, so this is the honest same-size comparison and the margin is a rounding error, not an upset. Claude rows are blank on this benchmark.

benchmarks.name: FrontierScience Olympiad
benchmarks.config: Same table, column 'FS Olympiad'. Reproduction 85.0 vs paper 86.0 (-1.0pp). WINS vs GPT-5.6 Sol 79.0, Agents-A1 79.0, GPT-5.5 78.0, DeepSeek-V4-Pro Preview 76.0 and Kimi-K2.6 73.0. TIES Gemini 3.1 Pro at 85.0 - a tie, not a win. No prior FS Olympiad row in the catalog, so there is no beaten catalog best to claim.

benchmarks.name: FrontierScience Research
benchmarks.config: Same table, column 'FS Research'. Reproduction 55.0 vs paper 56.7 (-1.7pp). WINS vs Agents-A1 40.0, Kimi-K2.6 17.9, DeepSeek-V4-Pro Preview 13.3, Muse-Spark-1.0 38.0, Gemini 3.1 Pro 26.7, GPT-5.5 26.7; LOSSES to Apodex 1.1 Agent Team 63.3, GPT-5.6 Sol 63.3 and Claude rows are blank. No prior FS Research row in the catalog.

benchmarks.name: BioMysteryBench (human-difficult subset)
benchmarks.config: Same table, column 'BMB' - the card's footnote defines it as the human-difficult BioMysteryBench subset. Reproduction 35.3 == paper 35.3 (unchanged). Ties Apodex 1.1 Agent Team 35.3 and Gemini 3.1 Pro 35.3; WINS vs Apodex 1.1 ReAct 23.5; LOSSES to Claude Opus 5 49.4, Claude Fable 5 46.1 and GPT-5.6 Sol 47.1. No prior BMB row in the catalog.
